answers.itr: For income of FY 2025-26 (assessment year 2026-27), returns are filed in 2026 under section 139(1) of the Income-tax Act, 1961. [IT-DUE-FY2526] Filing on time is needed to choose the old regime if you have business income and to carry forward most losses. [IT-DUE-FY2526] ITR-1 (Sahaj) is the simplest return, for a resident (ordinarily resident) individual with total income up to ₹50 lakh from salary or pension, up to two house properties (raised from one property for AY 2026-27), other sources such as interest, agricultural income up to ₹5,000, and long-term capital gains under section 112A (listed shares/equity funds) up to ₹1.25 lakh. answers.ca: Small taxpayers are exempt: Notification 15/2025-Central Tax (17 September 2025) exempts registered persons whose aggregate turnover in a financial year is up to Rs 2 crore from filing the annual return for FY 2024-25 onwards; similar year-by-year exemptions were given for earlier years. [GST-RET-GSTR9] An annual return cannot be filed more than three years after its due date (section 44(2)). [GST-RET-GSTR9] In your return you must add the salaries from both Form 16s, claim the standard deduction only once, and pay any shortfall as self-assessment tax (with interest under sections 234B/234C if applicable) before filing.
